summary: Independent read-only review passes the design-spec gate for focused plan revision 20. All nine approved file paths, versions and SHA-256 values match approval packet r1, the registered contract and current artifacts; the packet and user receipt hashes match. The eight design-spec documents remain coherent on Electron main ownership of the exact app-launched OpenCode v2 serve child, named typed least-authority preload operations, preview isolation, truthful UX/permission/recovery states and distinct macOS/Windows evidence. This report rebinds the unchanged approved document set to the current plan and contract; it does not request renewed user approval or assert runtime compatibility or security enforcement.

approval_integrity.interpretation: The immutable approval-request packet and approved documents retain their pre-approval status wording and revision-18 references. The current linked SSOT is revision 20 and the separate exact-packet receipt records approval. Conditional prerequisites in those documents are satisfied through current bound reviews, receipt and handoffs; their historical labels do not require another user approval.

review_observations.assessment: Electron main owns trusted service/admission modules, window lifecycle, the exact app-launched foreground serve child and the version-matched client. Ambient/shared servers and an embedded-host substitution are excluded; identity, readiness/authentication and observed shutdown/reaping remain required probes.

Closed versioned named preload functions require main-side sender/frame/lifecycle/payload validation, context isolation, sandboxing and disabled Node integration. Raw channels, filesystem/process authority and sidecar URL credentials are prohibited. Preview has a separate context without privileged preload; navigation/popups, local resources, CSP and external opens require separate evidence. Browser HTTP/CORS/pairing is explicitly scoped apart from desktop authority.

Requested/effective/observed state, accepted versus effect-confirmed, stop-requested versus terminated, and window/tab closure versus process exit remain distinct. Unknown effects and event gaps are visible; dispatched mutations and stale permission decisions are not automatically replayed. Permission labels derive from current revision and matching receipts, with policy denial distinguished from user denial. Operations preserve local diagnostics/redaction and recovery limits.

Static inspection confirms the documented 61 primitive, 65 semantic and 37 component tokens, 44 variants and six component families. UX and components agree on receipt-bound permission labels, execution-neutral approval tone, stale read-only reconciliation, keyboard access, inline versus modal focus behavior, reduced motion, long paths and per-platform visual verification. Manifest/CSS are supporting source references, not additional files in the nine-file approval packet; the design validator and UI were not executed.

Development E2E, package building, exact-package E2E and renderer inspection have distinct macOS/Windows obligations. Windows behavior requires Windows execution; package and sidecar hashes and observed process effects bind receipts. Browser evidence, mocks, static review and Figma artifacts do not replace platform security/accessibility evidence. Storage/retention-dependent persistence remains held, while bounded synthetic probes/bootstrap are authorized; signing, public release, auto-update, user/global configuration and credentials, ambient services and external telemetry remain excluded.

limitations: No project tests, design validator, dependency installation, Electron process, OpenCode process or runtime probes were executed.
Package compatibility, per-OS binary provisioning, actual preload and preview security, accessibility, lifecycle and child reaping remain unverified implementation evidence.
The design-spec verdict does not replace the independent product gate, matching handoff checks, code review, running-app design QA or full AC-01–18 completion.

provenance.review_method: Independent local document inspection, byte-level SHA-256 comparison, JSON metadata inspection and exact gate-binding recomputation using the harness canonical JSON digest rules. No prior verdict was adopted as proof.
